summary: Gradual SSE output churn then final silence for long-chat sessions behind LB/proxy
description:
Issue summary: BrightWrite (enterprise) reports progressive slowdown of SSE streaming responses during long-chat sessions originating from their web client behind a corporate load balancer. After ~20–60s of normal token stream, chunk cadence degrades (increasing inter-chunk latency) and ultimately the stream stops sending data for 10–30s before the connection is closed by the client. This is not an immediate 5xx; it looks like a gradual drift in throughput leading to a silent stall and client timeout.

Impact: Multiple active sessions from BrightWrite saw interrupted chat generation in prod us-east. Reported as user-visible partial replies and increased perceived latency. Customer has traffic routed through an internal LB that reuses upstream connections (connection reuse/keepalive). Estimated 12 sessions per minute affected during peak.

Environment: prod us-east; Redwood hosted API (api.redwood.ai) -> internal edge proxy -> ALB (customer) -> customer web clients (multiplexed SSE tabs). Affected models: redwood-llama-13b-v2 and fallback quantized 7b variant.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Use BrightWrite web client with SSE streaming enabled and long system+user prompt (> 2500 tokens).
2) Ensure client sessions are multiplexed (multiple tabs) and routed through their corporate LB that does connection reuse.
3) Observe normal streaming for ~20–60s, then token emission rate drops progressively and eventually the stream goes silent.
4) Client times out and reconnects, sometimes resuming with a new session but losing prior in-flight context.

Observed behavior:
- Inter-chunk delay grows from ~50–200ms to multiple seconds before stream silence.
- No immediate 5xx from Redwood; upstream edges show continuous TCP keepalive but little application-level bytes.
- Customer-side LB logs show backend connection persistent with occasional zero-byte writes; LB reports 'http downstream keepalive reused' around same timestamps.
- When customer repro from outside their LB (direct to Redwood edge), issue is much less frequent.

Expected behavior: steady token cadence until generation completes or server closes normally.

Attachments/logs:
- Customer-provided client-side trace (x-request-id: rw-req-8b3f-20260310)
- Edge request logs: https://logs.redwood.company/edge/rw-req-8b3f-20260310
- Sample server-side token-delay histogram (attached as snippet in comments)

Notes: This differs from a plain mid-token abort or instant disconnect; the failure profile looks like gradual resource throttling or buffer coalescing somewhere in the request path.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 Maya Lopez: Initial customer report received. They attached a client HAR and server x-request-id (rw-req-8b3f-20260310). Customer says this started after a new LB config changed idle timeouts last week.
2026-03-10 10:45 Dylan Moore: Acknowledged. Assigned to me for triage. Asked customer for curl reproduce with --no-buffer and SSE client details. Also asked SRE to pull edge traces for x-request-id.

2026-03-10 11:20 SRE (Priya Patel): Edge trace shows steady small data writes from runtime then a window where application-level bytes drop ~18s before client closes. No 5xx. Kernel retransmit counts spiked on one edge pod at same time. Linking trace: https://traces.redwood.company/trace/8b3f

2026-03-11 09:05 Dylan Moore: Reproduced locally against prod edge with a client-side proxy that simulates LB connection reuse. Observed identical progressive chunk delay. When bypassing the proxy, stream cadence remained steady. Hypothesis: connection reuse + proxy buffering/aggregation causing TCP write coalescing and application-facing backpressure due to small write patterns from runtime's chunking strategy.

2026-03-11 14:40 Platform Eng (Ravi Kapoor): Looked at serving-runtime token flushing. We batch small token fragments into ~256B writes. Under some kernel/TCP stack scenarios and when intermediate proxy reuses connections, the proxy aggregates until Nagle or socket buffer thresholds trigger, creating perceived stall. Also saw a pattern where the proxy performs header-only health checks that briefly pause data flow when reuse occurs.

2026-03-12 08:23 Dylan Moore: Sent customer a temporary workaround: enable chunked flush on their LB (disabling aggregation) or change LB idle/reuse settings to avoid long-lived reuse for SSE endpoints. Customer to try and report back.

2026-03-12 16:02 BrightWrite (Elena Park): Confirmed enabling 'proxy_preserve_chunked' reduced incidents in canary environment. Will schedule a config change to prod later today. Asked if Redwood can implement server-side mitigation for clients where changing LB is not possible.

2026-03-13 09:10 Platform Eng (Ravi Kapoor): Proposed server-side mitigations: 1) switch runtime to emit larger token coalesced packets for SSE endpoints when it detects intermediate proxy reuse; 2) add periodic keepalive NOP event (every 8s) when token cadence slows to keep proxy from aggregating. Creating follow-up internal ticket INT-44122 for runtime change.

2026-03-13 15:30 Dylan Moore: Drafting customer communication: provided recommended LB settings and ETA for server-side patch. Marking this ticket In Progress while INT-44122 tracks the runtime change.
investigation_notes:
Reproduce notes: Local repro succeeded only when client path included a proxy that reuses keepalive connections and aggregates small writes (mimic customer LB behavior). Direct connections rarely reproduce.

Metrics observed:
- Token_emit_latency: median increased from 60ms -> 1.8s during incidents.
- Edge pod kernel retransmit spike correlated with stream silence windows.
- No increase in runtime OOMs or worker crashes. Scheduler evictions were not elevated.

Hypotheses considered:
- Serving runtime backpressure gating due to KV cache locks: disproved (no KV lock logs).
- Worker GC spike causing pause: disproved (GC traces normal).
- Proxy/LB socket buffer coalescing (likely): supported by customer config change result.
- HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 or ALPN negotiation mismatch causing intermittent buffering: under investigation; customer uses HTTP/1.1 for SSE.

Temporary mitigation validated: Customer setting 'preserve_chunked: true' on LB reduced frequency from ~15% sessions to <1% in canary. This strongly implicates proxy-level aggregation.

Next steps:
- INT-44122: Implement server-side keepalive NOPs for streaming SSE when small-token pattern detected. Target: canary patch 2026-03-18.
- Add runtime heuristic to detect downstream proxy aggregation and switch to larger chunk writes.
- SRE to add alert for token_emit_latency 95th percentile crossing 800ms for SSE endpoints.
resolution: Partial workaround provided to customer: change LB setting to preserve chunked responses (confirmed canary improvement). Server-side mitigations planned: (1) runtime patch to emit periodic small NOP SSE events every 8s when token cadence drops; (2) heuristic to coalesce token writes into larger app-level writes when downstream proxy reuse is detected. INT-44122 created to track runtime work. Customer agreed to defer full rollout until after their maintenance window.
workaround: Customer instructed to enable chunked-preserve mode on LB or adjust keepalive reuse timeout. Alternative: client can reconnect with resume token after 10s silence (client-side).
follow_up_actions: INT-44122 - runtime change to emit periodic SSE NOPs (target canary 2026-03-18)
SRE: add token_emit_latency alert for SSE endpoints (threshold p95 800ms)
Postmortem if incidents reoccur at scale - link pending
